design.concept: A one-column inbox for the manager: the number of expenses waiting for a decision comes first, then each pending expense as a card with a full-width status strip, who registered it, the date, the category and the amount large. Each card ends in one large button that goes straight to the analysis, so the common case is one glance and one tap.
design.decisions: One view, so no scene host. The only task is to go and decide, and the decision itself lives on the team expenses page that abrirAnaliseDespesas opens. The decisionFirst template forbids a table or a list with column headers, so I used the big-number metric for the total and plain cards for the board; I did not use the vertical record list or the table molecule. Each card opens with a full-width colored status strip (warning for awaiting decision, info when it is a resubmission), using the status tokens. The outcome button sits at the bottom of the compact card, which is where the decision starts on this page; there are no facts below it. Amount and date are the largest values. Loading shows skeleton cards. Empty shows a large icon, one sentence and a refresh action. Errors show above the board in body color with a retry button. 'Load more' appears when the list says it has more pages. Nothing is computed on the page. Dates and the total are only formatted with Intl, and the amount is shown as the contract delivers it.
